context: A grandpa tells his young grandson an old folktale
purpose: Teach: 皇帝/将軍/英雄/知性/変身/予言/弔/願望

lines.speaker: goro_grandpa
lines.jp: 今夜はな、昔この国を治めていた皇帝の話をしてやろう。
lines.en: Tonight, I'll tell you the tale of an emperor who once ruled this land.
lines.style: Warm grandfatherly storytelling voice, slow and deliberate pacing

lines.speaker: sho_child
lines.jp: 皇帝って、王様より偉いの?
lines.en: An emperor? Is that greater than a king?
lines.style: Curious child voice, wide-eyed and eager to hear more

lines.speaker: goro_grandpa
lines.jp: そうとも。その下に強い将軍がいてな、戦に出れば必ず勝つ英雄として民に慕われていたんじゃ。
lines.en: Indeed. Beneath him served a mighty shogun, beloved by the people as a hero who never lost a battle.
lines.style: Gentle nostalgic tone, weaving the tale with affection

lines.speaker: sho_child
lines.jp: かっこいい!その将軍は強いだけじゃなくて、頭もよかったの?
lines.en: Cool! Was the shogun smart too, not just strong?
lines.style: Excited child interjection, leaning in with wonder

lines.speaker: goro_grandpa
lines.jp: うむ、力だけでなく知性も並はずれていてな、ある夜、白い狐に変身する不思議な老人と出会ったそうじゃ。
lines.en: Yes, his intellect was extraordinary too. One night, he met a mysterious old man who could transform into a white fox.
lines.style: Lowered voice, building mystery into the folktale atmosphere

lines.speaker: goro_grandpa
lines.jp: その老人は将軍に予言を残した。「お前は若くして倒れる」とな。
lines.en: The old man left the shogun a prophecy: 'You shall fall while still young.'
lines.style: Solemn dramatic delivery, pausing for the weight of the words

lines.speaker: sho_child
lines.jp: ええっ、こわいよ、おじいちゃん…それで将軍はどうしたの?
lines.en: Whaat, that's scary, grandpa... so what did the shogun do?
lines.style: Frightened child voice, clutching at grandpa's sleeve

lines.speaker: goro_grandpa
lines.jp: 彼はの、死を恐れず、民を守りたいという願望だけを胸に戦い続けたのじゃ。
lines.en: He fought on without fearing death, holding only the wish to protect his people in his heart.
lines.style: Reverent admiring tone, honoring the hero's resolve

lines.speaker: goro_grandpa
lines.jp: そして最期の日、皇帝みずから弔いの言葉を述べたという。立派な男じゃったよ。
lines.en: And on his final day, even the emperor himself spoke words of mourning. He was a truly noble man.
lines.style: Softening reflective close, voice trailing into quiet reverence
